status: draft — pending the human media preview (Omar: design; Dr. Fady Hannah-Shmouni: scientific accuracy)
note: One line per still of what the moment teaches, the learner alt text, the scientific point the medical owner should check (priority order), and why a candidate was regenerated. Read by review/make-media-preview.py.

m1-p03.teaches: Skin as a neuro-immuno-endocrine organ: four units, three signalling routes (neighbouring cells, nerves, blood); mostly cell, tissue and animal evidence.
m1-p03.alt: A cross-section of skin showing the epidermis, dermis, fat layer and a hair follicle with its glands, with signals passing between cells, along a nerve and into a blood vessel.
m1-p03.regenerated: 2 times — style anchor, first candidate sat too low in the frame for the phone pane (house composition line tightened); then second candidate still too low (composition line tightened again)

m1-p06.teaches: The aesthetic exam as a systemic screen: thinning and bruising, coarse dry skin and acanthosis nigricans point to cortisol, thyroid and insulin; some signs mean prompt referral.
m1-p06.alt: Three magnified patches of skin — thin with a bruise, coarse and dry, velvety and dark — each linked to the gland it points to: an adrenal gland, the thyroid and the pancreas.
m1-p06.medicalCheck: Skin sign paired with gland: thin skin with bruising and the adrenal (cortisol excess); coarse dry skin and the thyroid; acanthosis nigricans and the pancreas (hyperinsulinaemia).
m1-p06.regenerated: 1 time — wrong sign-to-gland wiring (bruise->thyroid, dry->adrenal); glands low in frame

m1-p08.teaches: The Hormone Cell Atlas read hormone and receptor RNA cell by cell across human tissues: a map of predicted capacity, not measured hormone release.
m1-p08.alt: A grid of small tissue tiles with a skin tile at the centre, where some cells carry receptor cups and a few hold outlined granules, marking cells predicted to respond to or make a hormone.

m1-p11.teaches: A receptor on a map is where an efficacy question starts; skin enzymes change potency; only a human trial answers it (sunscreen and vitamin D as the example).
m1-p11.alt: A droplet on the skin reaches a cell's receptor while an enzyme reshapes a passing molecule, and a line leads to two matched groups of dots standing for a randomized trial.
m1-p11.regenerated: 1 time — trial motif rendered as stacked coins (reads as money)

m1-p13.teaches: Senescent cells stop dividing but keep secreting cytokines, enzymes and growth factors (the SASP); p16-positive cells become more common with age in human skin.
m1-p13.alt: On the left a cell divides into two; on the right a larger, flattened cell has stopped dividing and releases a cloud of small particles into the frayed fibres around it.

m1-p16.teaches: The levers with randomized trials: daily sunscreen (B) and topical retinoids (tretinoin, guide A; retinol C); senotherapies are biomarker pilots.
m1-p16.alt: A skin cross-section with a thin protective film turning back sun rays and a few drops soaking in, above dense, orderly collagen in the dermis.

m1-p17.teaches: Fictional case: senolytic supplements rest on mouse data and small human pilots; daily sunscreen and topical retinoids have randomized trials with visible outcomes.
m1-p17.alt: Three steps of evidence, from a culture dish to a mouse to a human trial; an unmarked capsule sits on the mouse step, while a sun-protection film sits on the top step.

m2-p02.teaches: Skin regenerates cortisol from cortisone with 11β-HSD1, more with age and sun exposure; cortisol slows collagen synthesis; visible ageing in people is untested.
m2-p02.alt: A magnified skin cell in which an enzyme turns an inactive hormone into its active form, surrounded by thin, sparse collagen fibres.
m2-p02.regenerated: 1 time — copied the anchor's follicle/nerve/vessel, key-shaped tokens, no sparse collagen

m2-p06.teaches: 'Cortisol face': take the glucocorticoid history, look for discriminating features, reassure most, and route the few to formal testing and an endocrinologist.
m2-p06.alt: A stream of tokens passes under a lens; most continue into a calm pool, while a few violet tokens turn onto a path toward a small building.

m2-p08.teaches: Estrogen receptors sit in all skin; topical estradiol raised collagen in sun-protected but not photoaged skin; skin collagen falls with years since menopause.
m2-p08.alt: Two panels of dermis: in sun-protected skin, receptor-bearing cells lay down new collagen; in sun-damaged skin, the same cells sit among fragmented, clumped fibres with no new collagen.
m2-p08.regenerated: 1 time — anchor's violet nerve and vessel copied into both panels — violet in the photoaged panel reads as new collagen

m2-p11.teaches: US and UK menopausal hormone therapy is approved for symptoms and bone protection; the 2025–26 US label changes did not add skin; compounded 'bioidentical' products lack data.
m2-p11.alt: An open frame holds rising heat lines and a piece of spongy bone, while a small block of skin sits outside it, drawn in grey.
m2-p11.medicalCheck: Two of the approved uses drawn (vasomotor symptoms, bone); vulvovaginal symptoms are left to the text.

m2-p13.teaches: Some inherited endocrine syndromes show on the skin first: MEN1 angiofibromas, Carney complex lentigines and myxomas, MEN2A lichen amyloidosis before thyroid cancer.
m2-p13.alt: An upper back seen from behind with a rippled, pigmented patch between the shoulder blades, linked by a fine line to a drawing of the thyroid gland.
m2-p13.medicalCheck: Only the MEN2A example is drawn: interscapular cutaneous lichen amyloidosis linked to the thyroid.
m2-p13.regenerated: 1 time — front view, patch on the chest instead of between the shoulder blades (wrong site)

m2-p15.teaches: Everyday endocrine signs: adrenal darkening in creases, fast or virilising hirsutism, acanthosis nigricans, pretibial myxoedema, cold dry hypothyroid skin.
m2-p15.alt: Three body-part outlines with typical sites marked: the palm creases, a velvety patch at the back of the neck, and a raised plaque on the front of the shin.
m2-p15.medicalCheck: Three of the named signs drawn: palm creases (adrenal), acanthosis nigricans at the back of the neck, a pretibial plaque; hirsutism and hypothyroid skin are left to the text.
m2-p15.regenerated: 2 times — legs run off the frame; shin markers under the phone transport bar; then full figure again ran to the bottom; shin markers under the phone transport bar

m2-p17.teaches: Fictional case: lip and canthal lentigines, an eyelid papule and a father's heart tumour suggest Carney complex; specialist assessment before any laser.
m2-p17.alt: A pedigree with an affected father and daughter, a patch of skin with small dark spots and a soft bump, and a heart with a small mass in its left upper chamber, linked by one line.
m2-p17.medicalCheck: Pedigree shows an affected father and daughter (mother unaffected). Redrawn at review: the myxoma now sits in the left atrium (the upper chamber on the viewer's right of a textbook four-chamber cutaway, beside the pulmonary-vein openings), the commoner site; it is drawn as a small stalked mass by the septum reaching toward the mitral valve.
m2-p17.regenerated: 2 times — pedigree shaded the mother too (implies she is affected); then coordinator review — myxoma sat in the right atrium; redrawn in the left atrium (commoner site in Carney complex)

m3-p02.teaches: Dermal white adipose tissue: a fat layer inside the dermis, in cones around follicles in humans; antimicrobial in mice; its part in human skin ageing is unmeasured.
m3-p02.alt: A skin cross-section in which a cone of small fat cells surrounds the lower hair follicle inside the dermis, separate from the fat layer beneath.
m3-p02.regenerated: 2 times — anchor arcs/nerve copied in violet, pink surface line (second hue); then cone beside, not around, the follicle

m3-p04.teaches: Glycation: sugars bind collagen and end as AGEs that cross-link and stiffen the matrix; RAGE signalling in lab studies; the causal link to visible ageing is graded D.
m3-p04.alt: On the left, parallel collagen fibres lie free; on the right, the same fibres carry small sugar rings and are tied together by short cross-links.
m3-p04.regenerated: 1 time — atom letter 'O' drawn inside each sugar ring (text in pixels)

m3-p08.teaches: GLP-1 and GIP are incretins; native GLP-1 is cleared within minutes by DPP-4; semaglutide and tirzepatide are engineered to last, for approved indications.
m3-p08.alt: On the left an enzyme clips a pair of units off the end of a natural hormone chain; on the right a modified chain with an altered unit and a fatty tail resists the enzyme and stays whole.
m3-p08.medicalCheck: DPP-4 drawn clipping the two N-terminal residues off native GLP-1; the drug drawn with a substituted second residue and a fatty side chain. Confirm this is acceptable for semaglutide and tirzepatide at this level of detail.
m3-p08.regenerated: 2 times — enzyme cut the chain mid-way instead of removing the two end residues; then three beads clipped instead of two (DPP-4 removes a dipeptide)

m3-p12.teaches: On GLP-1 drugs: counsel before treatment, photograph with consent during, refer restoration requests; restoration advice is expert opinion.
m3-p12.alt: A path passes two blank conversation cards, a camera pointed at a blank frame, and an open door into another room.

m3-p13.teaches: Fictional case: facial volume loss and shedding on an effective, approved GLP-1 drug — counsel, record and refer; whether to stop belongs with her prescriber.
m3-p13.alt: Two cross-sections of cheek tissue over bone: one with a full fat pad under the skin, the other with a thinner pad and looser skin above it.
m3-p13.medicalCheck: Facial fat drawn as one pad over bone; real anatomy has separate superficial and deep compartments.

m3-p15.teaches: Inflammaging and the gut hypothesis: bacterial LPS crossing a leaky barrier, shown in mice and briefly after a fatty meal; not shown to drive skin disease.
m3-p15.alt: Two views of the gut lining: one with closed junctions keeping small bacterial fragments out, the other with loosened junctions letting them pass into a blood vessel.

m3-p18.teaches: Gut and skin: diet quality, metabolic care and established skin treatment come first; a zonulin test cannot show a leaky gut; gut-repair peptides last, if at all.
m3-p18.alt: A row of stepping stones leads from a plate of whole foods, past a small block of skin, to a single unmarked capsule on the last, smallest stone.
m3-p18.regenerated: 1 time — plate (first priority) sits under the phone transport bar; green hue

m4-p03.teaches: GHK-Cu: a plasma tripeptide that binds copper; the proposed copper-delivery and gene-expression mechanism comes largely from its discoverer's group.
m4-p03.alt: A three-bead peptide holds a copper ion, with fine lines toward the collagen fibres and enzymes it is proposed to supply.
m4-p03.medicalCheck: GHK-Cu drawn as three beads with the copper ion against the first two (Gly-His). Schematic only; confirm.
m4-p03.regenerated: 1 time — four beads drawn for a tripeptide; anchor follicles/gland copied into background

m4-p06.teaches: Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation (C); injected GHK-Cu has no trials, irritates tissue, and in the US sits outside the Category 1 listing.
m4-p06.alt: Two skin cross-sections: drops resting on the surface on the left, and a deposit deep in the dermis with a ring of irritated tissue on the right.

m4-p08.teaches: Three families — signal peptides, SNAP-25 mimics, oral collagen — all have trial records; the question that matters most is who funded them.
m4-p08.alt: Three vignettes: a fatty-tailed peptide near a skin fibroblast, a peptide at a nerve-muscle junction, and a collagen chain breaking into small pieces in the gut.

m4-p11.teaches: Cosmetic, supplement, drug: in the US and UK, cosmetic peptides and oral collagen reach sale without proving efficacy; only drugs pass an approval gate.
m4-p11.alt: Three lanes: a droplet and a capsule pass freely, while a tablet waits at a violet barrier across the third lane.
m4-p11.regenerated: 2 times — gates overlapped the supplement lane (implies supplements face approval); then violet gate still spanned the supplement lane

m4-p13.teaches: BPC-157 rests on rodent studies and case series; TB-500 is a seven-residue fragment of thymosin β4, never trialled; KPV is α-MSH's end tripeptide with no human RCT.
m4-p13.alt: A mouse on a lab plinth, a long peptide chain with a short fragment lifted out, and a shorter chain with its last three beads set apart.
m4-p13.medicalCheck: TB-500 drawn as a seven-bead fragment lifted from the first half of a long chain (residues 17–23 of thymosin β4); KPV as the last three beads of α-MSH.

m4-p17.teaches: Fictional case: a research-use-only three-peptide blend and new patchy pigmentation; no trial tests the blend; impurity and mislabelling are documented.
m4-p17.alt: A tangle of three different peptides with stray specks among them, linked to a skin cross-section where pigment cells at the base of the epidermis are crowded with dark granules.

m5-p02.teaches: The follicle runs its own stress axis and GH/IGF-1 loop; local DHT drives pattern hair loss; alopecia areata follows the collapse of immune privilege.
m5-p02.alt: A hair follicle with a closed feedback loop drawn around its bulb, which sits inside a faint protective shell that keeps nearby immune cells out.

m5-p05.teaches: Work up hair loss first — pattern, trigger, patches, androgens; minoxidil (men and women) and finasteride (men) have pooled trial support; refer severe alopecia areata.
m5-p05.alt: Four views of the scalp from above: thinning at the crown and front, even thinning everywhere, one round bare patch, and a widened central parting.
m5-p05.medicalCheck: Four hair-loss patterns seen from above: male pattern, diffuse shedding, an alopecia areata patch, female-pattern widened parting. The front of three ovals is bare (forehead).

m5-p07.teaches: POMC yields ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin; five melanocortin receptors (pigment, adrenal, two in the brain, sebum); which receptors a drug reaches decides its effects.
m5-p07.alt: A precursor peptide cut into three pieces above a row of five receptor tiles: a pigment cell, an adrenal gland, the brain twice, and a sebaceous gland.
m5-p07.medicalCheck: Five receptor tiles: MC1R pigment cell, MC2R adrenal, MC3R and MC4R brain (drawn twice), MC5R sebaceous gland — the tidy map the moment itself qualifies.
m5-p07.regenerated: 2 times — two separate brains drawn for the two brain receptors; then two adrenal glands drawn; precursor shattered into many pieces

m5-p10.teaches: Melanotan II harms come from case reports: darkening and new naevi, nail bands, melanomas without proven causation, and systemic emergencies.
m5-p10.alt: A patch of skin with darkened, varied moles and a crop of new small ones, beside a fingernail with a dark band running along its length.

m5-p11.teaches: Fictional case: tanning-peptide injections, new and darker naevi, a nail band and a mother with melanoma — an absolute contraindication in the guide.
m5-p11.alt: A mother-and-daughter pedigree with the mother marked, a patch of skin with darker and new moles, and a fingernail with a dark band.

m5-p14.teaches: PTD-DBM keeps CXXC5 off Dishevelled so Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises; hair regrew in mice (developer's group); zinc thymulin has no defined mechanism.
m5-p14.alt: Inside a cell, a small decoy peptide keeps a brake protein from docking on a signalling protein, and small signal tokens move into the nucleus.
m5-p14.medicalCheck: Most complex mechanism in the set: a cell-penetrating decoy peptide sits in the docking site so the grey 'brake' protein (CXXC5) cannot bind Dishevelled, and β-catenin tokens move into the nucleus. Confirm this reading of PTD-DBM (Lee 2017).

m5-p17.teaches: A compounded hair spray: thymulin is in US Category 3, PTD-DBM on no list, both grade D; in the UK an unlicensed special; return to diagnosis and approved options.
m5-p17.alt: A violet path passes under a magnifying lens to an open doorway, while a dashed side branch stops at a closed gate.
m5-p17.regenerated: 1 time — scalp became a face (eyes, nose); main route started at the closed gate

m6-p02.teaches: GH acts mainly on dermal fibroblasts; fibroblast-made IGF-1 drives keratinocytes to divide; GH and IGF-1 fall steadily with age (the somatopause).
m6-p02.alt: A skin cross-section where growth hormone from a capillary reaches fibroblasts in the dermis, which send smaller signals up to dividing cells at the base of the epidermis.

m6-p05.teaches: GH deficiency is a diagnosis; the fall with age is not. In healthy older adults GH brings small body-composition shifts and more side effects; distributing it for anti-ageing is a US federal offence.
m6-p05.alt: Two views of the pituitary: one pressed by a mass and releasing nothing, the other intact but releasing only a few small droplets.
m6-p05.medicalCheck: Deficiency drawn as a pituitary mass (one cause among several); normal ageing drawn as an intact gland releasing less.

m6-p07.teaches: One axis, four ways in: replace (somatropin), stimulate through the GHRH or ghrelin receptor, or bypass the pituitary with an IGF-1 analogue.
m6-p07.alt: A hormone axis from the brain to the pituitary, liver and tissue, with four violet entry points: two on the pituitary, one in the bloodstream and one at the tissue itself.
m6-p07.regenerated: 1 time — vertical axis ran to 92% of the height; tissue entry (bypass) hidden under the phone transport bar

m6-p12.teaches: Name the molecule (CJC-1295 with or without DAC), what evidence stands behind it, and where it stands legally; tesamorelin's A is for one HIV indication.
m6-p12.alt: Three cards in order: a bead-chain molecule, two columns of tokens standing for trial evidence, and a closed gate for regulatory status.

m6-p14.teaches: Sustained GH excess: thick, oily, sweaty skin, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans, enlarging hands and feet; the Endocrine Society advises IGF-1 when typical features appear.
m6-p14.alt: Two hands seen from the back, one of ordinary size and one broad and thick-fingered, each above a small skin section — the second thicker, with a swollen dermis and large pores.

m6-p17.teaches: Fictional case: tight rings, puffiness, night-time tingling, sweating and skin tags on a clinic 'CJC/ipamorelin' product — the soft-tissue pattern of GH excess.
m6-p17.alt: An open, puffy hand with a ring pressing into a swollen finger and fine wavy lines along the thumb, index and middle fingers suggesting tingling.
m6-p17.medicalCheck: Tingling drawn along the thumb, index and middle fingers (median nerve) to match carpal tunnel symptoms.

m7-p02.teaches: GRADE rates certainty for one outcome across the evidence: four levels; randomized trials start high, observational studies low; ratings move for named reasons.
m7-p02.alt: Four shelves of certainty: randomized trials start on the top shelf with one dot stepping down, observational studies lie on the third shelf, and a small cluster rests on the lowest.
m7-p02.medicalCheck: GRADE: randomized trials on the top shelf, observational studies on the third; the model also put a small cluster on the lowest shelf (very low). Keep, or redraw with the lowest shelf empty?
m7-p02.regenerated: 1 time — five shelves drawn (GRADE has four levels); coin stacks

m7-p05.teaches: Evidence grade and regulatory status are separate checks: an approval says nothing about the grade for an unapproved use, and a mechanism never raises a grade.
m7-p05.alt: A token travels a path through two different checkpoints in turn: a lens over trial evidence, then a gate bearing a blank seal.

m7-p07.teaches: US compounding: 503A is patient-specific, with a strict order for bulk substances (monograph, approved-drug component, bulks list); 503B facilities are GMP-inspected; both stay unapproved.
m7-p07.alt: A small counter preparing one item for one waiting person, beside a larger facility producing trays of identical items under an inspecting lens.
m7-p07.regenerated: 1 time — three human figures added (contract: no people in illustrations)

m7-p10.teaches: A certificate of analysis is the supplier's report on one lot — identity by mass spectrometry, purity by HPLC — and cannot prove origin, storage or sterility.
m7-p10.alt: A blank certificate linked to one tray of identical items, a lens revealing the molecule inside one of them, and a loose item whose link back to the tray is broken.

m7-p13.teaches: 'Research use only' is a US shipping permission for laboratory research; FDA reads intended use from claims and sale; it never makes a route to patients.
m7-p13.alt: A path from a laboratory bench ends at a closed gate with a blank tag hanging on it, before a clinic room with an empty couch.

m7-p22.teaches: In the UK, MHRA judges medicine status from claims, form and use; an unlicensed medicine may not be sold or advertised, and prescription-only medicines are never advertised to the public.
m7-p22.alt: A magnifying lens examines a plain phone screen showing a generic post, beside a megaphone blocked by a bar.
m7-p22.regenerated: 1 time — Instagram-style heart/comment/share icons on the phone (platform UI)

m7-p15.teaches: Off-label means an approved drug used outside its labelling; a never-approved peptide has no label to depart from; compounded products are also unapproved.
m7-p15.alt: On the left, a tablet with its leaflet steps just outside the leaflet's boundary; on the right, a tablet stands alone with no leaflet and no boundary.

m7-p17.teaches: Fictional case: 'off-label' BPC-157 — never approved, no 503A route; a certificate covers one lot's identity and purity, never sterility, storage or legality.
m7-p17.alt: A single item waits before a closed gate; a blank certificate lights only the item itself, leaving a thermometer and a sealed pouch outside its light.
m7-p17.regenerated: 1 time — large dark-grey shadow panel with a hard edge (breaks the light paper register)
